exposure: cell-free fetal DNA (cffDNA) concentration in maternal plasma
placenta previa (with or without placental adhesion/invasion)
outcome: abnormal placental invasion (placenta accreta, increta, percreta)
cohort: The study included 50 healthy singleton pregnant women carrying male fetuses, aged 20-40 years, para 1-5, with BMI 18-25 kg/m2, divided into a study group (n=25) with placenta previa and suspected placental adhesion/invasion and a matched control group (n=25) with normally situated placenta.
finding: There was no statistically significant difference regarding the level of free fetal DNA between the placenta accreta group and the control group, indicating no significant association between cffDNA and placenta accreta.
mod_finding: The placenta accreta group had a significantly higher number of Cesarean deliveries compared to the control group, with seven women in the placenta accreta group requiring cesarean hysterectomy.
cross-section timing: Blood samples for cell-free fetal DNA were collected between 28-34 weeks of gestation.
